threads.thread: Septic systems around Lake Paradise and Lake Mattoon
threads.summary: A resident raised concerns that older, grandfathered, or uninspected private septic systems near the two lakes may be discharging effluent into the water supply. Officials said they are working with the Coles County Health Department to begin inspecting private sewage systems around Lake Paradise, clarified that county public health departments hold jurisdiction rather than the EPA, and described starting in Coles County before coordinating with Cumberland and Shelby counties.
threads.commitment: Work with the Coles County Health Department to begin inspecting private sewage systems around Lake Paradise, then coordinate with Cumberland and Shelby counties.
threads.status: no further mention in the 5 meetings we have reviewed since

Septic System Jurisdiction & Inter-County Coordination: Council members discussed regulatory oversight of septic systems around the lakes, clarifying that public health departments hold jurisdiction rather than the EPA. Officials undertook to review the city ordinance against state regulations.

threads.thread: Watershed management planning for Lake Mattoon and Lake Paradise
threads.summary: The city engaged a consultant and formed a watershed management group to build a multi-year plan protecting the two source-water lakes. Commissioners reported on the group's kickoff meeting at the water treatment plant, a two-year structure of data collection followed by strategy implementation, a public planning meeting to set goals, and a third meeting on September 9 where data collection progress was said to support future grant applications.
threads.commitment: Carry out a two-year watershed management planning process with a consultant (year one data collection, year two strategy implementation), including public planning meetings at the water treatment plant.

threads.thread: Lake Mattoon flowage easements and sedimentation
threads.summary: Jason Little, a Lake Mattoon property owner residing in Neoga, raised the 1956 flowage easements and sediment accumulation that he said reduced water depth behind properties from 15 feet to under 3 feet, and noted the city's approximately $4.3 million in annual revenue from the lakes relative to costs borne by surrounding communities. Officials undertook to form a committee or small group to discuss easement rights and sedimentation with property owners.
threads.commitment: Form a committee or small group meeting to discuss Lake Mattoon easement rights and sedimentation concerns with property owners.
